verbatim_locators.note: ADV-218 part 2: complete read of the gnomAD v4.1.1 East Asian against non-Finnish European analysis, with the question whether any allele frequency bears on a registry statement about the reference genotype class or penetrance (answer in the result file).

entries.proposition: WWOX START-LOSS ALLELE c.2T>C: 4 of 40,686 East Asian alleles against 3 of 1,149,400 non-Finnish European alleles (ClinVar Pathogenic, one star); the reported OR 36.3 (9.0 to 146.9) and the uncorrected Fisher p of about 4.4 x 10^-5 were reproduced by the reader from the printed counts; the paper's q = 3.6 x 10^-3 is the Benjamini-Hochberg value over 805 tests.
entries.snippet: WWOX c.2T > C, a start-loss variant (4 of 40,686)

entries.proposition: THE PAPER STATES THE FOLD DIFFERENCE AND THE RANGE: five of the nine significant variants are 38 to 158 times more frequent in East Asians and four are absent from NFE; the WWOX start-loss allele is the 38-fold member.
entries.snippet: Four variants were absent from NFE; the other five showed EAS allele frequencies 38- to 158-fold higher than their NFE frequencies.

entries.proposition: TWO WWOX NONSENSE AND SPLICE ALLELES ARE EXPLORATORY ONLY: p.Glu171Ter (2 of 44,864) and c.172+1G>C (2 of 44,874), both absent from NFE; two alleles is the detection floor, they do not survive correction.
entries.snippet: These comprised AARS1 p. Arg330Ter (3 of 44,886), WWOX p. Glu171Ter (2 of 44,864), and WWOX c.172 + 1G > C (2 of 44,874).
entries.anchor: Results 3.4 Exploratory low-frequency signals and recessive-gene concentration

entries.proposition: WWOX p.Arg54Ter IS A DENOMINATOR EFFECT, NOT AN EXCESS OF EAST ASIAN CARRIERS: raw East Asian count 3 against 5 in NFE (about 26 times fewer East Asian alleles tested); the paper calls it East and South Asian enriched (SAS 3 of 91,068 in Supplementary Table S2).
entries.snippet: Two of the eight, WWOX p. Arg54Ter and KCNC1 p. Arg164Trp, had raw EAS counts that did not exceed their NFE counts.

entries.proposition: THE PAPER IS A FREQUENCY ANALYSIS, NOT A DISCOVERY OR PENETRANCE STUDY; WWOX is named among seven established recessive genes ('WWOX (epileptic encephalopathy)').
entries.snippet: Our study quantifies the East Asian population frequencies of their P/LP variants rather than claims their discovery.

entries.proposition: HOW FREQUENCY ENTERS INTERPRETATION IN THE PAPER: as a filter (a variant common in reference populations cannot cause fully penetrant severe early-onset disease), never as a penetrance estimate; no genotype, phenotype or segregation data are analysed.
entries.snippet: Population allele frequency is a cornerstone of this interpretation, because variants common in reference populations cannot cause fully penetrant, severe early-onset disease.

entries.proposition: THE ANALYSIS HAS A DETECTION FLOOR ABOUT 4.5 X 10^-5 IN EAST ASIANS and an asymmetric denominator; a missing East Asian signal below it proves nothing. Counts of two or three are sensitive to artefacts and relatedness.
entries.snippet: The EAS-NFE comparison is asymmetric in sample size and insensitive to EAS-specific enrichment below an allele frequency of about 4.5 × 10−5; negative findings below this floor do not imply equal frequencies.

entries.proposition: EXPLORATORY SIGNALS DID NOT SURVIVE CORRECTION: the authors state that counts of two or three are sensitive to sequencing artefacts and to relatives in gnomAD.
entries.snippet: The exploratory low-frequency signals did not survive multiple-testing correction, and their allele counts of two or three are sensitive to sequencing artifacts and the inclusion of related individuals in gnomAD.

entries.proposition: THE ALLELE-IDENTITY CLAIM THAT MATTERS FOR ANY WWOX FREQUENCY QUOTED FROM A RSID LOOKUP: 45 of 60 rsID-level candidates were false (one is WWOX p.Arg310Pro, whose most common allele at that position is p.Arg310His); a WWOX frequency taken from an rsID alone can belong to a different allele.
entries.snippet: Nucleotide-resolved matching confirmed only fifteen of these as genuine P/LP signals, corresponding to a false-positive rate of 45 of 60 (75.0%) (Figure 3).

entries.proposition: FIGURE 2 AS DRAWN: four WWOX points among the 17 (c.2T>C significant, East Asian allele frequency about 10^-4.0, 38-fold; p.Arg54Ter exploratory, about 10^-4.2, 16-fold; p.Glu171Ter and c.172+1G>C exploratory at the detection floor, NFE absent). Circles mark recessive genes.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2: WWOX c.2T>C red circle at EAS AF about 10^-4.0 with 38x; WWOX p.Arg54Ter orange circle at about 10^-4.2 with 16x; WWOX p.Glu171Ter and c.172+1G>C orange circles on the dashed detection floor with arrows (NFE absent); all WWOX points are circles (recessive).

entries.proposition: FIGURE 3 AS DRAWN: panel B Venn counts 15 confirmed, 45 false positives, 2 recovered; panel C bars 20, 20, 4, 1; the WWOX points of panel A lie between the 10-fold and 100-fold lines or at the left edge for NFE-absent alleles.
